changes.new: ### Operators, data nodes, and pipeline outputs The DALI example below reads an image and its mask through two branches. Each reader produces encoded files and labels; each decoder consumes the encoded files. The first reader's labels bypass the decoder and become a separate pipeline output. The second reader's labels are unused. The diagram distinguishes operators, which perform work, from `DataNode` objects, which connect an operator's output to another operator's input. ![[02 Areas/ML & DL/00 Учебник/Assets/Figures/curated/dali-2026-11-04/two_readers.svg|Two DALI FileReaders feed two ImageDecoders; decoded images, masks and the first reader's labels become pipeline outputs, while the second reader's labels are discarded]] *NVIDIA DALI, [Pipeline and processing graph — Data Processing Graphs](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DALI/blob/5b33fee1968ba069a9ed04965fd2af5f0025de7e/docs/pipeline.rst). Complete original vector, copied without cropping, relabeling or redrawing. [Apache-2.0 license](/licenses/nvidia-dali-5b33fee1-Apache-2.0.txt).* Original example, with the source's variable names and spacing: ```python @pipeline_def # create a pipeline with processing graph defined by the function below def my_pipeline(): """ Create a pipeline which reads images and masks, decodes the images and returns them. """ img_files, labels = fn.readers.file(file_root="image_dir", seed=1) mask_files, _ = fn.readers.file(file_root="mask_dir", seed=1) images = fn.decoders.image(img_files, device="mixed") masks = fn.decoders.image(mask_files, device="mixed") return images, masks, labels pipe = my_pipeline(batch_size=4, num_threads=2, device_id=0) ``` Calling `my_pipeline(batch_size=4, num_threads=2, device_id=0)` creates the pipeline object with those batch, thread and device settings. When DALI builds the graph, it executes the definition function once to connect data nodes; it does not decode the entire dataset. Running the pipeline produces successive batches through those connections. Returning `images, masks, labels` selects three outputs. DALI prunes subgraphs that do not contribute to an output, as described in [Current Pipeline](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DALI/blob/5b33fee1968ba069a9ed04965fd2af5f0025de7e/docs/pipeline.rst#current-pipeline). This is the documentation's file-reader example, not the preceding EDLS LMDB example. The image and mask directories must describe corresponding samples. The two `seed=1` arguments are not a validation of that correspondence: a missing mask or a different file order still requires a data check before training. The same graph also explains device placement. A CPU operator accepts CPU data and returns CPU data. A `mixed` operator accepts CPU inputs and returns GPU outputs, so both decoded image branches are already on the GPU. A GPU operator can consume those outputs without copying the decoded images back to the host. Named argument inputs may still come from CPU operators: the next example in [Processing Graph Structure](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DALI/blob/5b33fee1968ba069a9ed04965fd2af5f0025de7e/docs/pipeline.rst#processing-graph-structure) uses a CPU coin flip as the `horizontal` argument of a GPU `fn.flip`. To return the reader's labels on the GPU as well, that example explicitly returns `labels.gpu()`. The code requires NVIDIA DALI and the two input directories. It is reproduced to explain the graph; it was syntax-checked, not executed on a GPU. The figure supplies no timing result and does not establish that this pipeline is faster than a PyTorch loader.
